Write to CSV (write_to_csv): This function saves the section data (such as Experience, Education, etc.) to a CSV file. Each section is written as a new row, with columns for Candidate Name, Section, and Content.

Content Processing: The parsed resume sections like Experience, Education, and Skills are written to the CSV, while personal info (name, degree, etc.) is omitted for clarity.

Scalability: You can easily scale this approach to include more sections (e.g., Certifications, Publications, Languages) by expanding the extract_section function and adding columns in the CSV.

Downstream Use: For downstream tasks like analysis, filtering, or reporting, having each section in its row makes it easier to query or manipulate individual sections separately.

def process_resume(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    
    # Extract text depending on file type (PDF, Image)
    if ext in ['pdf']:
        text = extract_text(file_path)
    elif ext in ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png']:
        text = run_ocr(file_path)
    else:
        return None  # Unsupported file format
    
    # Extract structured data using NLP and regex
    parsed_data = extract_data_with_nlp(text, file_path)
    if parsed_data:
        # Save to CSV
        save_to_csv(parsed_data)

# Function to run OCR on images (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr(image_path):
    try:
        image = Image.open(image_path)
        text = pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
        return text
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error extracting text from image {image_path}: {e}")
        return None

# NLP-based extraction using spaCy and regex for specific fields
def extract_data_with_nlp(text, file_path):
    doc = nlp(text)
    
    first_name, last_name = extract_name(doc)
    degree = extract_degree(text)
    university = extract_university(text)
    linkedin = extract_linkedin(text)
    skills = extract_skills(text)

    # Validate and format the filename
    filename = format_filename(first_name, last_name, degree, university, file_path)
    
    # Prepare the parsed data
    parsed_data = {
        "Candidate Name": f"{first_name} {last_name}",
        "First Name": first_name,
        "Last Name": last_name,
        "Degree": degree,
        "University": university,
        "LinkedIn": linkedin,
        "Skills": skills,
        "Experience": extract_section(text, "Experience"),
        "Education": extract_section(text, "Education"),
        "LinkedIn Match Confidence": "Pending GPT validation"
    }
    return parsed_data

# Extract first and last name from resume text using spaCy
def extract_name(doc):
    for ent in doc.ents:
        if ent.label_ == "PERSON":
            name_parts = ent.text.split()
            return name_parts[0], name_parts[-1]  # Assume first and last name
    return "Unknown", "Unknown"

# Extract degree from the resume text
def extract_degree(text):
    if "bachelor" in text.lower():
        return "BS"
    if "master" in text.lower():
        return "MS"
    return "Unknown"

# Extract university from the resume text
def extract_university(text):
    universities = ["University of California", "State University of New York"]
    for university in universities:
        if university.lower() in text.lower():
            return university
    return "Unknown"

# Extract LinkedIn URL
def extract_linkedin(text):
    match = re.search(r"https?://(www\.)?linkedin\.com/in/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", text)
    return match.group(0) if match else "Unknown"

# Extract skills from the resume text
def extract_skills(text):
    skills = ["Python", "Java", "Machine Learning"]
    return [skill for skill in skills if skill.lower() in text.lower()]

# Extract specific section (e.g., Experience, Education)
def extract_section(text, section_name):
    pattern = re.compile(rf"({section_name}:)(.*?)(?=\n[A-Z])", re.DOTALL)
    match = re.search(pattern, text)
    if match:
        return match.group(2).strip()
    return "No content"

# Format the filename based on parsed data
def format_filename(first_name, last_name, degree, university, file_path):
    grad_date = extract_graduation_date(file_path)
    filename = f"{last_name}, {first_name} - {degree} - {university} ({grad_date})"
    return "".join(c for c in filename if c not in "\\/:*?\"<>|")

# Extract graduation date from resume text
def extract_graduation_date(file_path):
    # Example: May 2024 or Expected Graduation May 2024
    return "Unknown"

# Save parsed data to CSV
def save_to_csv(parsed_data):
    fieldnames = ["Candidate Name", "First Name", "Last Name", "Degree", "University", "LinkedIn", "Skills", "Experience", "Education", "LinkedIn Match Confidence"]
    
    # Save CSV file with formatted filename
    filename = format_filename(parsed_data["First Name"], parsed_data["Last Name"], parsed_data["Degree"], parsed_data["University"], parsed_data["Candidate Name"]) + ".csv"
    file_path = os.path.join(save_directory, filename)
    
    with open(file_path, mode='a', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        if file.tell() == 0:  # If file is empty, write the header
            writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerow(parsed_data)

# Watchdog Event Handler for folder monitoring
class ResumeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        
        # Process the resume file when a new one is added to the folder
        print(f"New resume detected: {event.src_path}")
        process_resume(event.src_path)

# Setup folder monitoring
def monitor_folder():
    event_handler = ResumeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, monitor_directory, recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor_folder()

Directory Setup:

Digital Resumes: These are PDF files that contain a text layer (i.e., text that can be extracted directly without OCR).

We will use PDF text extraction (via pdfminer or similar libraries).

Scanned Resumes: These are image-based files (e.g., JPG, PNG, or scanned PDFs) that do not have a text layer. For these, we will use OCR (Optical Character Recognition) to extract the text.

We will use Tesseract OCR for image-based resume processing.

Approach for Handling Digital vs. Scanned Resumes:
Detect whether the resume is digital or scanned:

Digital Resumes: If the file is a PDF and contains a text layer, we can directly extract the text using PDF extraction tools (like pdfminer).

Scanned Resumes: If the file is a scanned PDF or an image (JPG, PNG), we will use OCR to extract the text.

Process the resume based on its type:

Digital: Extract text directly using pdfminer or PyMuPDF.

Scanned: Run Tesseract OCR to extract text from the image or scanned content.

Step-by-Step Adjustments:
Determine Resume Type (Digital or Scanned):

We'll check if the file is a PDF and whether it has a text layer.

For image-based files (JPG, PNG), we’ll automatically treat them as scanned and run OCR.

Apply Appropriate Processing:

If the resume is digital, extract the text directly.

If the resume is scanned, use OCR to extract the text.

# Helper function to determine if the resume is digital or scanned
def is_scanned(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    
    # Check if the file is a PDF
    if ext == 'pdf':
        # Use PyMuPDF to check if the PDF has a text layer
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            if page.get_text("text"):  # Check if text is extracted from the page
                return False  # It's a digital (text-based) resume
    return True  # Treat as scanned if not a text-based PDF

# Function to process scanned resumes (images or scanned PDFs)
def process_scanned_resume(file_path):

    if ext in ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png']:

    if parsed_data:

The warning message you're seeing (CropBox missing from /Page, defaulting to MediaBox) is typically associated with PDFs that don't contain explicit crop box information. This is usually harmless and just indicates that the library is defaulting to the media box for page dimensions, which might result in slightly inaccurate page cropping or layout calculations when extracting text. However, this shouldn’t affect the ability to extract text from the PDF.

Potential Solutions:
Ignore the Warning: Since it’s just a warning, if the text extraction works fine and you can get the content from the PDF, you can safely ignore this message.

Fixing PDF Layout Issues: If the layout or text extraction is poor, you can try using a more advanced PDF library like PyMuPDF (fitz), which may handle this better.

Further Debugging: If you find that the text extraction quality is compromised, we can adjust the script to better handle these edge cases, or switch the library to something like PyMuPDF or even Tesseract OCR if we determine the PDF is more image-based.

How to Handle PDF Extraction Better
Since you are using pdfminer, let’s consider a few alternatives or improvements for better handling of PDFs, particularly when encountering such warnings.

1. Switch to PyMuPDF (fitz) for PDF Text Extraction
PyMuPDF (fitz) tends to handle PDF text extraction better in cases where pdfminer struggles. Here’s how you can modify the script to use PyMuPDF for extracting text:

Install PyMuPDF:

pip install pymupdf
Modify the Script to Use PyMuPDF:

import fitz  # PyMuPDF

# Function to extract text from a PDF using PyMuPDF
def extract_text_from_pdf(file_path):
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    text = ""
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        text += page.get_text("text")  # Extract text from the page
    return text
This code uses PyMuPDF to open the PDF and extract text from each page. PyMuPDF tends to work better for certain PDFs that may have layout issues or missing crop boxes.

2. Detect and Handle Image-Based PDFs Using OCR
If the PDF is more image-based (like scanned documents), you can switch to OCR extraction with Tesseract as a fallback, as you’re doing with image files.

Here’s how to handle scanned PDFs with OCR:

import pytesseract
from PIL import Image
import fitz  # PyMuPDF

# Function to handle scanned PDFs (Image-based PDFs)
def extract_text_from_scanned_pdf(file_path):
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    text = ""
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        # Convert PDF page to image
        pix = page.get_pixmap()
        img = Image.frombytes("RGB", [pix.width, pix.height], pix.samples)
        text += pytesseract.image_to_string(img)  # Run OCR on the image
    return text
In this approach:

PyMuPDF is used to convert each page of the scanned PDF into an image.

Tesseract OCR is then used to extract text from the image.

3. Add Error Handling for OCR PDFs
We can enhance the script to fall back to OCR if the PDF contains no text layer, thus covering all cases, whether the resume is digital or scanned.

# Function to check if the resume is scanned or digital
def is_scanned(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    
    # Check if the file is a PDF
    if ext == 'pdf':
        # Use PyMuPDF to check if the PDF has a text layer
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            if page.get_text("text"):  # Check if text is extracted from the page
                return False  # It's a digital (text-based) resume
    return True  # Treat as scanned if not a text-based PDF
If the file is a scanned PDF (or image-based), it will fall back to OCR, ensuring better text extraction for image-based resumes.

4. Final Integration
Now, the main function will automatically check if the resume is digital or scanned and process it accordingly.

def process_resume(file_path):
    if is_scanned(file_path):  # If scanned (image-based PDF or image file)
        process_scanned_resume(file_path)
    else:  # If digital (text-based PDF)
        process_digital_resume(file_path)

def extract_degree(text):

    return "Unknown"

def extract_linkedin(text):
    match = re.search(r"https?://(www\.)?linkedin\.com/in/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", text)
    return match.group(0) if match else "Unknown"

# Extract skills from the resume text
def extract_skills(text):
    skills = ["Python", "Java", "Machine Learning"]
    return [skill for skill in skills if skill.lower() in text.lower()]

def extract_section(text, section_name):
    pattern = re.compile(rf"({section_name}:)(.*?)(?=\n[A-Z])", re.DOTALL)
    match = re.search(pattern, text)
    if match:
        return match.group(2).strip()
    return "No content"

# Helper function to determine if the resume is digital or scanned
def is_scanned(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    
    # Check if the file is a PDF
    if ext == 'pdf':
        # Use PyMuPDF to check if the PDF has a text layer
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            if page.get_text("text"):  # Check if text is extracted from the page
                return False  # It's a digital (text-based) resume
    return True  # Treat as scanned if not a text-based PDF

# Function to process digital resumes (PDF with text layer)
def process_digital_resume(file_path):
    # Extract text from the digital resume PDF using PyMuPDF
    text = extract_text_from_pdf(file_path)
    return text

# Function to process scanned resumes (images or scanned PDFs)
def process_scanned_resume(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    text = ""
    if ext in ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png']:
        # If the file is an image (JPG/PNG), use OCR to extract text
        text = run_ocr(file_path)
    elif ext == 'pdf':
        # If the file is a scanned PDF, use OCR to extract text from each page
        text = run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path)
    
    return text

# Function to run OCR on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr(image_path):
    try:
        image = Image.open(image_path)
        text = pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
        return text
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error extracting text from image {image_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to run OCR on scanned PDFs (image-based PDFs)
def run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path):
    text = ""
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        # Convert PDF page to image
        pix = page.get_pixmap()
        img = Image.frombytes("RGB", [pix.width, pix.height], pix.samples)
        text += pytesseract.image_to_string(img)  # Run OCR on the image
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using PyMuPDF
def extract_text_from_pdf(file_path):
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    text = ""
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        text += page.get_text("text")  # Extract text from the page
    return text

# Watchdog Event Handler for folder monitoring
class ResumeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        
        # Process the resume file when a new one is added to the folder
        print(f"New resume detected: {event.src_path}")
        
        # Check if the resume is scanned or digital
        if is_scanned(event.src_path):  # If scanned (image-based PDF or image file)
            process_scanned_resume(event.src_path)
        else:  # If digital (text-based PDF)
            process_digital_resume(event.src_path)

# Setup folder monitoring
def monitor_folder():
    event_handler = ResumeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, monitor_directory, recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor_folder()

I think the issue is we are not doing any preprocesssing of the resume before extraction. We need to add stuff. SeWhat would you recommend to preprocess either a digital or scanned resume? 
ChatGPT said:
To effectively preprocess a resume before text extraction (whether it’s a digital PDF or a scanned document), we need to clean, normalize, and enhance the content to ensure we capture all relevant information for accurate extraction. Preprocessing helps improve the quality of text extraction, especially for resumes that may be poorly formatted or contain complex layouts.

Preprocessing Steps:
1. Remove Noise and Unnecessary Data:
Garbage Character Removal: Text from both digital PDFs and scanned PDFs often contains unnecessary artifacts or noise (e.g., corrupted characters, strange symbols, or headers/footers).

For digital PDFs: We can clean up the text to remove page numbers, footers, and headers.

For scanned PDFs: OCR results often have garbage characters that need to be cleaned.

Tools: Use regular expressions or text-cleaning libraries to remove unwanted characters.

2. Normalize Layout and Text Format:
Standardize Formatting: Resume layouts may vary, but it’s important to extract data from the same areas across resumes. For example, names might be at the top of the page, followed by education or experience.

For both digital and scanned resumes, we can:

Detect headings (e.g., Experience, Education) and normalize them.

Convert everything to lowercase for easier matching (e.g., matching "Bachelor of Science" with "bachelor of science").

Remove extra spaces and line breaks.

3. Language and Tokenization:
Text Tokenization: Break down the content into tokens (words or phrases) for further processing, especially useful for digital PDFs that might be split across columns or pages.

Spelling Correction: OCR often introduces errors in scanned documents. We can run a spell check or correction algorithm to fix common OCR mistakes (e.g., "engineer" misread as "enginneer").

NLP Techniques: Use spaCy or NLTK to detect and remove stop words, punctuation, and irrelevant words.

4. Handling Multi-column Text (for Digital PDFs):
Some digital PDFs have multi-column layouts that can break the text flow.

We need to flatten the columns into a single text flow, which can be done by checking the positions of the text blocks and concatenating them appropriately.

5. Handwriting Detection:
Scanned Resumes: Detect whether there is handwriting (e.g., a handwritten score) in the resume. This can be used to tag whether the candidate was met on campus or had a handwritten assessment.

For OCR: You can use handwriting density estimation (the percentage of handwritten content on the page) to determine whether it should be excluded from the parsing process or flagged for further review.

6. Section Detection:
Identify Key Sections: Resume sections (like Experience, Education, Skills, etc.) need to be clearly identified, especially if the resume format is unconventional. NLP-based methods can be used to:

Detect headings (e.g., "Experience", "Education").

Extract context around key terms.

For Scanned PDFs: You can use OCR-based layout analysis to detect these sections as well.

7. Text Summarization:
After extracting text from a scanned resume via OCR, you can apply a text summarizer to condense lengthy text into key points (e.g., skills, qualifications). This will make it easier to match against specific keywords like programming languages, certifications, or specific job roles.

Preprocessing for Digital vs. Scanned Resumes
For Digital Resumes (PDFs with Text Layer):
Text Extraction: Direct extraction from the PDF.

Text Cleanup: Remove headers/footers, page numbers, and extra white spaces.

Format Normalization: Normalize layout to ensure consistent formatting.

Tokenization: Split the text into sentences/words for easier extraction of entities.

Section Detection: Use spaCy or regex to identify sections like Experience and Education.

For Scanned Resumes (Image-based or Scanned PDFs):
OCR (Tesseract): Run OCR to extract text.

Noise Removal: Clean up OCR output by removing garbage characters.

Handwriting Detection: Detect and handle handwritten content (e.g., manually entered scores).

Section Detection: Use OCR and NLP to detect key sections (e.g., Experience, Education).

Text Summarization: Optionally summarize text for better results.

Suggested Preprocessing Pipeline:
Step 1: Detect Document Type (Digital or Scanned)

Check if the document is digital (PDF with a text layer) or scanned (image-based or scanned PDF).

Step 2: Text Extraction

For digital PDFs: Extract text using PyMuPDF or pdfminer.

For scanned PDFs/images: Run Tesseract OCR to extract text.

Step 3: Text Cleanup

Remove garbage characters, page numbers, headers, footers.

Normalize spaces and line breaks.

Step 4: Handwriting Detection (for scanned resumes)

Estimate handwriting density and detect any handwritten content (e.g., scores).

Step 5: Section Detection:

Use NLP (spaCy or regex) to detect sections like Experience, Education, and Skills.

Normalize section headings (e.g., "Experience" -> "Experience Section").

Step 6: Data Extraction:

Extract key entities such as name, degree, university, skills, and LinkedIn.

Step 7: Save and Output:

Save the cleaned and structured text to CSV or JSON for downstream processing.

    if ext == 'pdf':

        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            if page.get_text("text"):
                return False  # It's a digital (text-based) resume
    return True  # Treat as scanned if not a text-based PDF

# Function to clean up text (remove unwanted characters)
def clean_text(text):
    # Remove non-alphanumeric characters, unwanted page numbers, etc.
    text = re.sub(r'\n+', ' ', text)  # Collapse multiple newlines into one space
    text = re.sub(r'[^\x00-\x7F]+', '', text)  # Remove non-ASCII characters
    return text.strip()

# Function to process digital PDFs (PyMuPDF or pdfminer)
def process_digital_resume(file_path):
    text_pymupdf = extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path)
    text_pdfminer = extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path)
    
    # Compare both text results and clean them

# Function to process scanned PDFs (OCR)

    if file_path.lower().endswith(('jpg', 'jpeg', 'png')):
        # Process images using OCR
        text = run_ocr(file_path)
    elif file_path.lower().endswith('pdf'):
        # Process scanned PDF using OCR
        text = run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path)
    return clean_text(text)

# Helper function to determine if the resume is digital or scanned
def is_scanned(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    
    # Check if the file is a PDF
    if ext == 'pdf':
        # Use PyMuPDF to check if the PDF has a text layer
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            if page.get_text("text"):  # Check if text is extracted from the page
                return False  # It's a digital (text-based) resume
    return True  # Treat as scanned if not a text-based PDF

# Function to clean up text (remove unwanted characters)
def clean_text(text):
    # Remove non-alphanumeric characters, unwanted page numbers, etc.
    text = re.sub(r'\n+', ' ', text)  # Collapse multiple newlines into one space
    text = re.sub(r'[^\x00-\x7F]+', '', text)  # Remove non-ASCII characters
    text = re.sub(r'(\d{1,2}[:\-\s]+)', '', text)  # Remove page numbers or other number artifacts
    return text.strip()

# Function to process digital PDFs (PyMuPDF or pdfminer)
def process_digital_resume(file_path):
    # Extract text from the digital resume PDF using both PyMuPDF and pdfminer
    text_pymupdf = extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path)
    text_pdfminer = extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path)
    
    # Clean the extracted texts
    text_pymupdf = clean_text(text_pymupdf)
    text_pdfminer = clean_text(text_pdfminer)
    
    # Compare both text results and clean them
    text_to_process = compare_texts(text_pymupdf, text_pdfminer)
    return text_to_process

# Function to process scanned resumes (images or scanned PDFs)
def process_scanned_resume(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    text = ""
    if ext in ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png']:
        # If the file is an image (JPG/PNG), use OCR to extract text
        text = run_ocr(file_path)
    elif ext == 'pdf':
        # If the file is a scanned PDF, use OCR to extract text from each page
        text = run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path)
    
    # Clean the OCR text
    text = clean_text(text)
    return text

# Function to run OCR on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr(image_path):
    try:
        image = Image.open(image_path)
        text = pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
        return text
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error extracting text from image {image_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to run OCR on scanned PDFs (image-based PDFs)
def run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path):
    text = ""
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        # Convert PDF page to image
        pix = page.get_pixmap()
        img = Image.frombytes("RGB", [pix.width, pix.height], pix.samples)
        text += pytesseract.image_to_string(img)  # Run OCR on the image
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using PyMuPDF
def extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path):
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    text = ""
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        text += page.get_text("text")  # Extract text from the page
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using pdfminer
def extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path):
    return extract_text(file_path)

# Function to compare extracted texts and choose the best result
def compare_texts(text1, text2):
    # You can use more sophisticated comparison if needed, e.g., text similarity
    if len(text1) > len(text2):
        return text1
    return text2

# NLP-based extraction using spaCy and regex for specific fields
def extract_data_with_nlp(text):
    doc = nlp(text)
    first_name, last_name = extract_name(doc)
    degree = extract_degree(text)
    university = extract_university(text)
    linkedin = extract_linkedin(text)
    skills = extract_skills(text)
    experience = extract_section(text, "Experience")
    education = extract_section(text, "Education")
    
    return {
        "First Name": first_name,
        "Last Name": last_name,
        "Degree": degree,
        "University": university,
        "LinkedIn": linkedin,
        "Skills": skills,
        "Experience": experience,
        "Education": education
    }

def extract_name(doc):
    for ent in doc.ents:
        if ent.label_ == "PERSON":
            name_parts = ent.text.split()
            return name_parts[0], name_parts[-1]  # Assume first and last name
    return "Unknown", "Unknown"

def extract_degree(text):
    degree_patterns = [r"(bachelor|master|phd|doctor)", r"(b.s.|m.s.|bs|ms)"]
    for pattern in degree_patterns:
        if re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):
            return "BS"  # Simplify to a single degree for now
    return "Unknown"

def extract_university(text):
    universities = ["University of California", "State University of New York"]
    for university in universities:
        if university.lower() in text.lower():
            return university
    return "Unknown"

def extract_linkedin(text):
    match = re.search(r"https?://(www\.)?linkedin\.com/in/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", text)
    return match.group(0) if match else "Unknown"

def extract_skills(text):
    skills = ["Python", "Java", "Machine Learning"]
    return [skill for skill in skills if skill.lower() in text.lower()]

def extract_section(text, section_name):
    pattern = re.compile(rf"({section_name}:)(.*?)(?=\n[A-Z])", re.DOTALL)
    match = re.search(pattern, text)
    if match:
        return match.group(2).strip()
    return "No content"

def format_filename(first_name, last_name, degree, university, file_path):
    grad_date = extract_graduation_date(file_path)
    filename = f"{last_name}, {first_name} - {degree} - {university} ({grad_date})"
    return "".join(c for c in filename if c not in "\\/:*?\"<>|")

def extract_graduation_date(file_path):
    # Example: May 2024 or Expected Graduation May 2024
    return "Unknown"

def save_to_csv(parsed_data, file_path):
    fieldnames = ["First Name", "Last Name", "Degree", "University", "LinkedIn", "Skills", "Experience", "Education"]
    
    filename = f"{parsed_data['Last Name']}, {parsed_data['First Name']} - {parsed_data['Degree']} - {parsed_data['University']} ({parsed_data['Graduation Date']}).csv"
    
    with open(filename, mode='w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerow(parsed_data)

# Watchdog Event Handler for folder monitoring
class ResumeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        
        # Process the resume file when a new one is added to the folder
        print(f"New resume detected: {event.src_path}")
        
        # Check if the resume is scanned or digital
        if is_scanned(event.src_path):  # If scanned (image-based PDF or image file)
            process_scanned_resume(event.src_path)
        else:  # If digital (text-based PDF)
            process_digital_resume(event.src_path)

# Setup folder monitoring
def monitor_folder():
    event_handler = ResumeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, monitor_directory, recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor_folder()

The time it takes for the script to process a resume depends on several factors:

Resume Type:

Digital PDFs (with a text layer) should process faster because the text can be extracted directly using PyMuPDF or pdfminer.

Scanned PDFs (image-based) or image files (JPG, PNG) require OCR (Tesseract) to extract text, which generally takes longer, especially for large documents.

File Size:

Larger resumes with more pages or more content will take longer to process. The extraction time increases with the number of pages and complexity of the layout.

System Resources:

The speed of text extraction depends on your machine’s performance (CPU, memory). OCR (Tesseract) is particularly resource-intensive when dealing with image-based content.

Time Estimates:
Digital PDFs: Extracting text using PyMuPDF or pdfminer typically takes a few seconds per page. A simple 1-3 page PDF might take 5-10 seconds.

Scanned PDFs/Images (OCR): OCR can take significantly longer. It may take 30 seconds to 1 minute per page, depending on the quality of the image, complexity of the document, and OCR accuracy. A 3-page scanned resume could take 1-3 minutes.

Why You Might Be Seeing Warnings:
The warnings CropBox missing from /Page, defaulting to MediaBox are informational messages from PyMuPDF when it doesn’t find crop box information in the PDF. These warnings don’t affect the extraction process but may indicate that the document’s layout may not be fully optimized.

If you're seeing delays, it could be due to:

Large File Size: If the resume has many pages or is highly formatted.

OCR Processing: If it's a scanned PDF or image, OCR might take a bit longer.

2. Add Timeout for OCR (for scanned resumes):
OCR processing (especially for scanned PDFs or images) can take a long time, depending on the file size and complexity. If OCR is causing the script to hang, we can add a timeout to prevent it from running indefinitely.

Example: Add Timeout for OCR
You can add a timeout to the OCR function using the concurrent.futures module to ensure that it doesn't hang forever:

import concurrent.futures

# Function to run OCR with timeout
def run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=30):
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        future = executor.submit(pytesseract.image_to_string, Image.open(image_path))
        try:
            text = future.result(timeout=timeout)  # Set timeout to 30 seconds
            return text
        except concurrent.futures.TimeoutError:
            print(f"OCR processing for {image_path} took too long, skipping...")
            return "OCR Timeout"

# Modify run_ocr to use the new function with a timeout
def run_ocr(image_path):
    return run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=30)  # 30 seconds timeout
This will ensure that if the OCR processing takes longer than 30 seconds, it will be skipped, and the script will continue processing.

            img = Image.frombytes("RGB", [pix.width, pix.height], pix.samples)
            text += pytesseract.image_to_string(img)  # Run OCR on the image
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error running OCR on PDF {file_path}: {e}")
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using PyMuPDF
def extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path):
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    text = ""
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        text += page.get_text("text")  # Extract text from the page
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using pdfminer
def extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path):
    return extract_text(file_path)

# Function to compare extracted texts and choose the best result
def compare_texts(text1, text2):
    # You can use more sophisticated comparison if needed, e.g., text similarity
    if len(text1) > len(text2):
        return text1
    return text2

# NLP-based extraction using spaCy and regex for specific fields
def extract_data_with_nlp(text):
    doc = nlp(text)
    first_name, last_name = extract_name(doc)
    degree = extract_degree(text)
    university = extract_university(text)
    linkedin = extract_linkedin(text)
    skills = extract_skills(text)
    experience = extract_section(text, "Experience")
    education = extract_section(text, "Education")
    
    return {

        "Last Name": last_name,
        "Degree": degree,
        "University": university,
        "LinkedIn": linkedin,
        "Skills": skills,
        "Experience": experience,
        "Education": education
    }

def extract_name(doc):
    for ent in doc.ents:
        if ent.label_ == "PERSON":
            name_parts = ent.text.split()
            return name_parts[0], name_parts[-1]  # Assume first and last name
    return "Unknown", "Unknown"

def extract_degree(text):
    degree_patterns = [r"(bachelor|master|phd|doctor)", r"(b.s.|m.s.|bs|ms)"]
    for pattern in degree_patterns:
        if re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):
            return "BS"  # Simplify to a single degree for now
    return "Unknown"

def extract_university(text):
    universities = ["University of California", "State University of New York"]
    for university in universities:
        if university.lower() in text.lower():
            return university
    return "Unknown"

def extract_linkedin(text):
    match = re.search(r"https?://(www\.)?linkedin\.com/in/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", text)
    return match.group(0) if match else "Unknown"

def extract_skills(text):
    skills = ["Python", "Java", "Machine Learning"]
    return [skill for skill in skills if skill.lower() in text.lower()]

def extract_section(text, section_name):
    pattern = re.compile(rf"({section_name}:)(.*?)(?=\n[A-Z])", re.DOTALL)
    match = re.search(pattern, text)
    if match:
        return match.group(2).strip()
    return "No content"

def format_filename(first_name, last_name, degree, university, file_path):
    grad_date = extract_graduation_date(file_path)
    filename = f"{last_name}, {first_name} - {degree} - {university} ({grad_date})"
    return "".join(c for c in filename if c not in "\\/:*?\"<>|")

def extract_graduation_date(file_path):
    # Example: May 2024 or Expected Graduation May 2024
    return "Unknown"

def save_to_csv(parsed_data, file_path):
    fieldnames = ["First Name", "Last Name", "Degree", "University", "LinkedIn", "Skills", "Experience", "Education"]
    
    filename = f"{parsed_data['Last Name']}, {parsed_data['First Name']} - {parsed_data['Degree']} - {parsed_data['University']} ({parsed_data['Graduation Date']}).csv"
    
    with open(filename, mode='w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerow(parsed_data)

# Watchdog Event Handler for folder monitoring
class ResumeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        
        # Process the resume file when a new one is added to the folder
        print(f"New resume detected: {event.src_path}")
        
        # Check if the resume is scanned or digital
        if is_scanned(event.src_path):  # If scanned (image-based PDF or image file)
            process_scanned_resume(event.src_path)
        else:  # If digital (text-based PDF)
            process_digital_resume(event.src_path)

# Setup folder monitoring
def monitor_folder():
    event_handler = ResumeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, monitor_directory, recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor_folder()

# Helper function to determine if the resume is digital or scanned
def is_scanned(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    
    # Check if the file is a PDF
    if ext == 'pdf':
        # Use PyMuPDF to check if the PDF has a text layer
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            if page.get_text("text"):  # Check if text is extracted from the page
                return False  # It's a digital (text-based) resume
    return True  # Treat as scanned if not a text-based PDF

# Function to clean up text (remove unwanted characters)
def clean_text(text):
    # Remove non-alphanumeric characters, unwanted page numbers, etc.
    text = re.sub(r'\n+', ' ', text)  # Collapse multiple newlines into one space
    text = re.sub(r'[^\x00-\x7F]+', '', text)  # Remove non-ASCII characters
    text = re.sub(r'(\d{1,2}[:\-\s]+)', '', text)  # Remove page numbers or other number artifacts
    return text.strip()

# Function to process digital PDFs (PyMuPDF or pdfminer)
def process_digital_resume(file_path):
    try:
        print(f"Processing digital resume: {file_path}")
        # Extract text from the digital resume PDF using both PyMuPDF and pdfminer
        text_pymupdf = extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path)
        text_pdfminer = extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path)
        
        # Clean the extracted texts
        text_pymupdf = clean_text(text_pymupdf)
        text_pdfminer = clean_text(text_pdfminer)
        
        # Compare both text results and clean them
        text_to_process = compare_texts(text_pymupdf, text_pdfminer)
        return text_to_process
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing digital resume {file_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to process scanned resumes (images or scanned PDFs)
def process_scanned_resume(file_path):
    try:
        print(f"Processing scanned resume: {file_path}")
        ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
        text = ""
        
        if ext in ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png']:
            # If the file is an image (JPG/PNG), use OCR to extract text
            text = run_ocr(file_path)
        elif ext == 'pdf':
            # If the file is a scanned PDF, use OCR to extract text from each page
            text = run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path)
        
        # Clean the OCR text
        text = clean_text(text)
        return text
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing scanned resume {file_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to run OCR with timeout on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=OCR_TIMEOUT):
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        future = executor.submit(pytesseract.image_to_string, Image.open(image_path))
        try:
            text = future.result(timeout=timeout)  # Set timeout for OCR
            return text
        except concurrent.futures.TimeoutError:
            print(f"OCR processing for {image_path} took too long, skipping...")
            return "OCR Timeout"

# Function to run OCR on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr(image_path):
    return run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=OCR_TIMEOUT)  # 30 seconds timeout for OCR

# Function to run OCR on scanned PDFs (image-based PDFs)
def run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path):
    text = ""
    try:
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            # Convert PDF page to image
            pix = page.get_pixmap()
            img = Image.frombytes("RGB", [pix.width, pix.height], pix.samples)
            text += pytesseract.image_to_string(img)  # Run OCR on the image
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error running OCR on PDF {file_path}: {e}")
    return text

            return "OCR Timeout"

# Function to run OCR on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr(image_path):
    return run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=OCR_TIMEOUT)  # 30 seconds timeout for OCR

# Function to run OCR on scanned PDFs (image-based PDFs)
def run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path):
    text = ""
    try:
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            # Convert PDF page to image
            pix = page.get_pixmap()
            img = Image.frombytes("RGB", [pix.width, pix.height], pix.samples)
            text += pytesseract.image_to_string(img)  # Run OCR on the image
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error running OCR on PDF {file_path}: {e}")
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using PyMuPDF
def extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path):
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    text = ""
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        text += page.get_text("text")  # Extract text from the page
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using pdfminer
def extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path):
    return extract_text(file_path)

    # You can use more sophisticated comparison if needed, e.g., text similarity
    if len(text1) > len(text2):

    return text2

def extract_name(doc):
    for ent in doc.ents:
        if ent.label_ == "PERSON":
            name_parts = ent.text.split()
            return name_parts[0], name_parts[-1]  # Assume first and last name
    return "Unknown", "Unknown"

def extract_degree(text):
    degree_patterns = [r"(bachelor|master|phd|doctor)", r"(b.s.|m.s.|bs|ms)"]
    for pattern in degree_patterns:
        if re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):
            return "BS"  # Simplify to a single degree for now
    return "Unknown"

def extract_university(text):
    universities = ["University of California", "State University of New York"]
    for university in universities:
        if university.lower() in text.lower():
            return university
    return "Unknown"

def extract_linkedin(text):
    match = re.search(r"https?://(www\.)?linkedin\.com/in/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", text)
    return match.group(0) if match else "Unknown"

def extract_skills(text):
    skills = ["Python", "Java", "Machine Learning"]
    return [skill for skill in skills if skill.lower() in text.lower()]

def extract_section(text, section_name):
    pattern = re.compile(rf"({section_name}:)(.*?)(?=\n[A-Z])", re.DOTALL)
    match = re.search(pattern, text)
    if match:
        return match.group(2).strip()
    return "No content"

def format_filename(first_name, last_name, degree, university, file_path):
    grad_date = extract_graduation_date(file_path)
    filename = f"{last_name}, {first_name} - {degree} - {university} ({grad_date})"
    return "".join(c for c in filename if c not in "\\/:*?\"<>|")

def extract_graduation_date(file_path):
    # Example: May 2024 or Expected Graduation May 2024
    return "Unknown"

def save_to_csv(parsed_data, file_path):
    fieldnames = ["First Name", "Last Name", "Degree", "University", "LinkedIn", "Skills", "Experience", "Education"]
    
    filename = f"{parsed_data['Last Name']}, {parsed_data['First Name']} - {parsed_data['Degree']} - {parsed_data['University']} ({parsed_data['Graduation Date']}).csv"
    
    with open(filename, mode='w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerow(parsed_data)

# Watchdog Event Handler for folder monitoring
class ResumeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        
        # Process the resume file when a new one is added to the folder
        print(f"New resume detected: {event.src_path}")
        
        # Check if the resume is scanned or digital
        if is_scanned(event.src_path):  # If scanned (image-based PDF or image file)
            process_scanned_resume(event.src_path)
        else:  # If digital (text-based PDF)
            process_digital_resume(event.src_path)

# Setup folder monitoring
def monitor_folder():
    event_handler = ResumeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, monitor_directory, recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor_folder()

# Initialize spaCy for Named Entity Recognition (NER)
nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

# Define the directories to monitor and save CSV files

# Helper function to determine if the resume is digital or scanned
def is_scanned(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    
    # Check if the file is a PDF
    if ext == 'pdf':
        # Use PyMuPDF to check if the PDF has a text layer
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            if page.get_text("text"):  # Check if text is extracted from the page
                return False  # It's a digital (text-based) resume
    return True  # Treat as scanned if not a text-based PDF

# Function to clean up text (remove unwanted characters)
def clean_text(text):
    # Remove non-alphanumeric characters, unwanted page numbers, etc.
    text = re.sub(r'\n+', ' ', text)  # Collapse multiple newlines into one space
    text = re.sub(r'[^\x00-\x7F]+', '', text)  # Remove non-ASCII characters
    text = re.sub(r'(\d{1,2}[:\-\s]+)', '', text)  # Remove page numbers or other number artifacts
    return text.strip()

# Function to process digital PDFs (PyMuPDF or pdfminer)
def process_digital_resume(file_path):
    try:
        print(f"Processing digital resume: {file_path}")
        # Extract text from the digital resume PDF using both PyMuPDF and pdfminer
        text_pymupdf = extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path)
        text_pdfminer = extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path)
        
        # Clean the extracted texts
        text_pymupdf = clean_text(text_pymupdf)
        text_pdfminer = clean_text(text_pdfminer)
        
        # Compare both text results and clean them
        text_to_process = compare_texts(text_pymupdf, text_pdfminer)
        return text_to_process
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing digital resume {file_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to process scanned resumes (images or scanned PDFs)
def process_scanned_resume(file_path):
    try:
        print(f"Processing scanned resume: {file_path}")
        ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
        text = ""
        
        if ext in ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png']:
            # If the file is an image (JPG/PNG), use OCR to extract text
            text = run_ocr(file_path)
        elif ext == 'pdf':
            # If the file is a scanned PDF, use OCR to extract text from each page
            text = run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path)
        
        # Clean the OCR text
        text = clean_text(text)
        return text
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing scanned resume {file_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to run OCR with timeout on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=OCR_TIMEOUT):
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        future = executor.submit(pytesseract.image_to_string, Image.open(image_path))
        try:
            text = future.result(timeout=timeout)  # Set timeout for OCR
            return text
        except concurrent.futures.TimeoutError:
            print(f"OCR processing for {image_path} took too long, skipping...")
            return "OCR Timeout"

# Function to run OCR on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr(image_path):
    return run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=OCR_TIMEOUT)  # 30 seconds timeout for OCR

        print(f"Error running OCR on PDF {file_path}: {e}")
    return text

def save_to_csv(parsed_data, file_path):
    fieldnames = ["First Name", "Last Name", "Degree", "University", "LinkedIn", "Skills", "Experience", "Education"]
    
    filename = f"{parsed_data['Last Name']}, {parsed_data['First Name']} - {parsed_data['Degree']} - {parsed_data['University']} ({parsed_data['Graduation Date']}).csv"

# Watchdog Event Handler for folder monitoring
class ResumeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        
        # Process the resume file when a new one is added to the folder
        print(f"New resume detected: {event.src_path}")
        
        # Check if the resume is scanned or digital
        if is_scanned(event.src_path):  # If scanned (image-based PDF or image file)
            process_scanned_resume(event.src_path)
        else:  # If digital (text-based PDF)
            process_digital_resume(event.src_path)

# Setup folder monitoring
def monitor_folder():
    event_handler = ResumeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, monitor_directory, recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor_folder()

import os
import time
import csv
import spacy
import pytesseract
from watchdog.observers import Observer
from watchdog.events import FileSystemEventHandler
from pdfminer.high_level import extract_text
from PIL import Image
import re
import fitz  # PyMuPDF for handling PDFs
import concurrent.futures

# Initialize spaCy for Named Entity Recognition (NER)
nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

# Define the directories to monitor and save CSV files
monitor_directory = r"C:\Users\goblu\Downloads\RESUME EXTRACTION FILES\GPT Split Process\Drop Resumes Here"
save_directory = r"C:\Users\goblu\Downloads"

# Set timeout duration for OCR processing (in seconds)
OCR_TIMEOUT = 30  # Timeout for OCR processing (30 seconds)

# Max file size limit (in MB) to avoid hanging on large files
MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB = 50  # Max file size limit for PDFs and images

# Helper function to determine if the resume is digital or scanned
def is_scanned(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    
    # Check if the file is a PDF
    if ext == 'pdf':
        # Use PyMuPDF to check if the PDF has a text layer
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            if page.get_text("text"):  # Check if text is extracted from the page
                return False  # It's a digital (text-based) resume
    return True  # Treat as scanned if not a text-based PDF

# Function to clean up text (remove unwanted characters)
def clean_text(text):
    # Remove non-alphanumeric characters, unwanted page numbers, etc.
    text = re.sub(r'\n+', ' ', text)  # Collapse multiple newlines into one space
    text = re.sub(r'[^\x00-\x7F]+', '', text)  # Remove non-ASCII characters
    text = re.sub(r'(\d{1,2}[:\-\s]+)', '', text)  # Remove page numbers or other number artifacts
    return text.strip()

# Function to process digital PDFs (PyMuPDF or pdfminer)
def process_digital_resume(file_path):
    try:
        print(f"Starting to process digital resume: {file_path}")
        # Extract text from the digital resume PDF using both PyMuPDF and pdfminer
        text_pymupdf = extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path)
        text_pdfminer = extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path)
        
        # Clean the extracted texts
        text_pymupdf = clean_text(text_pymupdf)
        text_pdfminer = clean_text(text_pdfminer)
        
        # Compare both text results and clean them
        text_to_process = compare_texts(text_pymupdf, text_pdfminer)
        print(f"Processed text for digital resume: {file_path}")
        return text_to_process
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing digital resume {file_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to process scanned resumes (images or scanned PDFs)
def process_scanned_resume(file_path):
    try:
        print(f"Starting to process scanned resume: {file_path}")
        ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
        text = ""
        
        if ext in ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png']:
            # If the file is an image (JPG/PNG), use OCR to extract text
            text = run_ocr(file_path)
        elif ext == 'pdf':
            # If the file is a scanned PDF, use OCR to extract text from each page
            text = run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path)
        
        # Clean the OCR text
        text = clean_text(text)
        print(f"Processed text for scanned resume: {file_path}")
        return text
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing scanned resume {file_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to run OCR with timeout on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=OCR_TIMEOUT):
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        future = executor.submit(pytesseract.image_to_string, Image.open(image_path))
        try:
            text = future.result(timeout=timeout)  # Set timeout for OCR
            return text
        except concurrent.futures.TimeoutError:
            print(f"OCR processing for {image_path} took too long, skipping...")
            return "OCR Timeout"

# Function to run OCR on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr(image_path):
    print(f"Running OCR on {image_path}...")
    return run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=OCR_TIMEOUT)  # 30 seconds timeout for OCR

# Function to run OCR on scanned PDFs (image-based PDFs)
def run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path):
    text = ""
    try:
        print(f"Running OCR on scanned PDF: {file_path}...")
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            # Convert PDF page to image
            pix = page.get_pixmap()
            img = Image.frombytes("RGB", [pix.width, pix.height], pix.samples)
            text += pytesseract.image_to_string(img)  # Run OCR on the image
        print(f"OCR completed for scanned PDF: {file_path}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error running OCR on PDF {file_path}: {e}")
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using PyMuPDF
def extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path):
    print(f"Extracting text using PyMuPDF from {file_path}...")
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    text = ""
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        text += page.get_text("text")  # Extract text from the page
    print(f"Text extracted using PyMuPDF from {file_path}")
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using pdfminer
def extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path):
    print(f"Extracting text using pdfminer from {file_path}...")
    text = extract_text(file_path)
    print(f"Text extracted using pdfminer from {file_path}")
    return text

# Function to compare extracted texts and choose the best result
def compare_texts(text1, text2):
    # You can use more sophisticated comparison if needed, e.g., text similarity
    if len(text1) > len(text2):
        return text1
    return text2

# NLP-based extraction using spaCy and regex for specific fields
def extract_data_with_nlp(text):
    doc = nlp(text)
    first_name, last_name = extract_name(doc)
    degree = extract_degree(text)
    university = extract_university(text)
    linkedin = extract_linkedin(text)
    skills = extract_skills(text)
    experience = extract_section(text, "Experience")
    education = extract_section(text, "Education")
    
    return {
        "First Name": first_name,
        "Last Name": last_name,
        "Degree": degree,
        "University": university,
        "LinkedIn": linkedin,
        "Skills": skills,
        "Experience": experience,
        "Education": education
    }

def extract_name(doc):
    for ent in doc.ents:
        if ent.label_ == "PERSON":
            name_parts = ent.text.split()
            return name_parts[0], name_parts[-1]  # Assume first and last name
    return "Unknown", "Unknown"

def extract_degree(text):
    degree_patterns = [r"(bachelor|master|phd|doctor)", r"(b.s.|m.s.|bs|ms)"]
    for pattern in degree_patterns:
        if re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):
            return "BS"  # Simplify to a single degree for now
    return "Unknown"

    universities = ["University of California", "State University of New York"]
    for university in universities:
        if university.lower() in text.lower():
            return university
    return "Unknown"

    full_path = os.path.join(save_directory, filename)
    
    with open(full_path, mode='w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerow(parsed_data)
    print(f"CSV saved as {full_path}")

# Watchdog Event Handler for folder monitoring
class ResumeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        
        # Process the resume file when a new one is added to the folder
        print(f"New resume detected: {event.src_path}")
        
        # Check if the resume is scanned or digital
        if is_scanned(event.src_path):  # If scanned (image-based PDF or image file)
            process_scanned_resume(event.src_path)
        else:  # If digital (text-based PDF)
            process_digital_resume(event.src_path)

# Setup folder monitoring
def monitor_folder():
    event_handler = ResumeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, monitor_directory, recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor_folder()

import os
import time
import csv
import spacy
import pytesseract
from watchdog.observers import Observer
from watchdog.events import FileSystemEventHandler
from pdfminer.high_level import extract_text
from PIL import Image
import re
import fitz  # PyMuPDF for handling PDFs
import concurrent.futures

# Initialize spaCy for Named Entity Recognition (NER)
nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

# Define the directories to monitor and save CSV files
monitor_directory = r"C:\Users\goblu\Downloads\RESUME EXTRACTION FILES\GPT Split Process\Drop Resumes Here"
save_directory = r"C:\Users\goblu\Downloads"  # CSV output directory

# Set timeout duration for OCR processing (in seconds)
OCR_TIMEOUT = 30  # Timeout for OCR processing (30 seconds)

# Max file size limit (in MB) to avoid hanging on large files
MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB = 50  # Max file size limit for PDFs and images

# Helper function to determine if the resume is digital or scanned
def is_scanned(file_path):
    ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
    
    # Check if the file is a PDF
    if ext == 'pdf':
        # Use PyMuPDF to check if the PDF has a text layer
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            if page.get_text("text"):  # Check if text is extracted from the page
                return False  # It's a digital (text-based) resume
    return True  # Treat as scanned if not a text-based PDF

# Function to clean up text (remove unwanted characters)
def clean_text(text):
    # Remove non-alphanumeric characters, unwanted page numbers, etc.
    text = re.sub(r'\n+', ' ', text)  # Collapse multiple newlines into one space
    text = re.sub(r'[^\x00-\x7F]+', '', text)  # Remove non-ASCII characters
    text = re.sub(r'(\d{1,2}[:\-\s]+)', '', text)  # Remove page numbers or other number artifacts
    return text.strip()

# Function to process digital PDFs (PyMuPDF or pdfminer)
def process_digital_resume(file_path):
    try:
        print(f"Starting to process digital resume: {file_path}")
        # Extract text from the digital resume PDF using both PyMuPDF and pdfminer
        text_pymupdf = extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path)
        text_pdfminer = extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path)
        
        # Clean the extracted texts
        text_pymupdf = clean_text(text_pymupdf)
        text_pdfminer = clean_text(text_pdfminer)
        
        # Compare both text results and clean them
        text_to_process = compare_texts(text_pymupdf, text_pdfminer)
        print(f"Processed text for digital resume: {file_path}")
        return text_to_process
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing digital resume {file_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to process scanned resumes (images or scanned PDFs)
def process_scanned_resume(file_path):
    try:
        print(f"Starting to process scanned resume: {file_path}")
        ext = file_path.lower().split('.')[-1]
        text = ""
        
        if ext in ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png']:
            # If the file is an image (JPG/PNG), use OCR to extract text
            text = run_ocr(file_path)
        elif ext == 'pdf':
            # If the file is a scanned PDF, use OCR to extract text from each page
            text = run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path)
        
        # Clean the OCR text
        text = clean_text(text)
        print(f"Processed text for scanned resume: {file_path}")
        return text
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing scanned resume {file_path}: {e}")
        return None

# Function to run OCR with timeout on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=OCR_TIMEOUT):
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        future = executor.submit(pytesseract.image_to_string, Image.open(image_path))
        try:
            text = future.result(timeout=timeout)  # Set timeout for OCR
            return text
        except concurrent.futures.TimeoutError:
            print(f"OCR processing for {image_path} took too long, skipping...")
            return "OCR Timeout"

# Function to run OCR on image files (e.g., JPG, PNG)
def run_ocr(image_path):
    print(f"Running OCR on {image_path}...")
    return run_ocr_with_timeout(image_path, timeout=OCR_TIMEOUT)  # 30 seconds timeout for OCR

# Function to run OCR on scanned PDFs (image-based PDFs)
def run_ocr_on_pdf(file_path):
    text = ""
    try:
        print(f"Running OCR on scanned PDF: {file_path}...")
        doc = fitz.open(file_path)
        for page_num in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc.load_page(page_num)
            # Convert PDF page to image
            pix = page.get_pixmap()
            img = Image.frombytes("RGB", [pix.width, pix.height], pix.samples)
            text += pytesseract.image_to_string(img)  # Run OCR on the image
        print(f"OCR completed for scanned PDF: {file_path}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error running OCR on PDF {file_path}: {e}")
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using PyMuPDF
def extract_text_from_pdf_pymupdf(file_path):
    print(f"Extracting text using PyMuPDF from {file_path}...")
    doc = fitz.open(file_path)
    text = ""
    for page_num in range(len(doc)):
        page = doc.load_page(page_num)
        text += page.get_text("text")  # Extract text from the page
    print(f"Text extracted using PyMuPDF from {file_path}")
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using pdfminer
def extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path):
    print(f"Extracting text using pdfminer from {file_path}...")
    text = extract_text(file_path)
    print(f"Text extracted using pdfminer from {file_path}")
    return text

# Function to compare extracted texts and choose the best result
def compare_texts(text1, text2):
    # You can use more sophisticated comparison if needed, e.g., text similarity
    if len(text1) > len(text2):
        return text1
    return text2

# NLP-based extraction using spaCy and regex for specific fields
def extract_data_with_nlp(text):
    doc = nlp(text)
    first_name, last_name = extract_name(doc)
    degree = extract_degree(text)
    university = extract_university(text)
    linkedin = extract_linkedin(text)
    skills = extract_skills(text)
    experience = extract_section(text, "Experience")
    education = extract_section(text, "Education")
    
    return {
        "First Name": first_name,
        "Last Name": last_name,
        "Degree": degree,
        "Major": "Unknown",  # Defaulting major to Unknown for simplicity
        "University": university,
        "Graduation Date": "Unknown",  # Defaulting Graduation Date to Unknown
        "LinkedIn": linkedin,
        "Skills": skills,
        "Experience": experience,
        "Education": education
    }

def extract_name(doc):
    for ent in doc.ents:
        if ent.label_ == "PERSON":
            name_parts = ent.text.split()
            return name_parts[0], name_parts[-1]  # Assume first and last name
    return "Unknown", "Unknown"

def extract_degree(text):
    degree_patterns = [r"(bachelor|master|phd|doctor)", r"(b.s.|m.s.|bs|ms)"]
    for pattern in degree_patterns:
        if re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):
            return "BS"  # Simplify to a single degree for now
    return "Unknown"

def extract_university(text):
    universities = ["University of California", "State University of New York"]
    for university in universities:
        if university.lower() in text.lower():
            return university
    return "Unknown"

def extract_linkedin(text):
    match = re.search(r"https?://(www\.)?linkedin\.com/in/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", text)
    return match.group(0) if match else "Unknown"

def extract_skills(text):
    skills = ["Python", "Java", "Machine Learning"]
    return [skill for skill in skills if skill.lower() in text.lower()]

def extract_section(text, section_name):
    pattern = re.compile(rf"({section_name}:)(.*?)(?=\n[A-Z])", re.DOTALL)
    match = re.search(pattern, text)
    if match:
        return match.group(2).strip()
    return "No content"

def format_filename(first_name, last_name, degree, university, file_path):
    grad_date = extract_graduation_date(file_path)
    filename = f"{last_name}, {first_name} - {degree} - {university} ({grad_date})"
    return "".join(c for c in filename if c not in "\\/:*?\"<>|")

def extract_graduation_date(file_path):
    # Example: May 2024 or Expected Graduation May 2024
    return "Unknown"

def save_parsed_data_to_csv(parsed_data):
    # Define the filename using the structured data
    filename = f"{parsed_data['Last Name']}, {parsed_data['First Name']} - {parsed_data['Degree']} - {parsed_data['Major']} - {parsed_data['University']} ({parsed_data['Graduation Date']}).csv"
    
    # Define the CSV file path
    csv_file_path = os.path.join(save_directory, filename)
    
    # Define CSV headers
    fieldnames = ["First Name", "Last Name", "Degree", "Major", "University", "Graduation Date", "LinkedIn", "Skills", "Experience", "Education"]
    
    # Create and write data to CSV
    with open(csv_file_path, mode='w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerow(parsed_data)
    print(f"CSV saved successfully: {csv_file_path}")

# Watchdog Event Handler for folder monitoring
class ResumeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        
        # Process the resume file when a new one is added to the folder
        print(f"New resume detected: {event.src_path}")
        
        # Check if the resume is scanned or digital
        if is_scanned(event.src_path):  # If scanned (image-based PDF or image file)
            process_scanned_resume(event.src_path)
        else:  # If digital (text-based PDF)
            process_digital_resume(event.src_path)

# Setup folder monitoring
def monitor_folder():
    event_handler = ResumeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, monitor_directory, recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor_folder()

    print(f"Text extracted using PyMuPDF from {file_path}")
    return text

# Extract text from a PDF using pdfminer
def extract_text_from_pdf_pdfminer(file_path):
    print(f"Extracting text using pdfminer from {file_path}...")
    text = extract_text(file_path)
    print(f"Text extracted using pdfminer from {file_path}")
    return text

# Function to compare extracted texts and choose the best result
def compare_texts(text1, text2):
    # You can use more sophisticated comparison if needed, e.g., text similarity
    if len(text1) > len(text2):
        return text1
    return text2

# NLP-based extraction using spaCy and regex for specific fields
def extract_data_with_nlp(text):
    doc = nlp(text)
    first_name, last_name = extract_name(doc)
    degree = extract_degree(text)
    university = extract_university(text)
    linkedin = extract_linkedin(text)
    skills = extract_skills(text)
    experience = extract_section(text, "Experience")
    education = extract_section(text, "Education")
    
    # Debug print to verify parsed data before saving to CSV
    print(f"Parsed Data: First Name: {first_name}, Last Name: {last_name}, Degree: {degree}, University: {university}")
    
    return {
        "First Name": first_name,
        "Last Name": last_name,
        "Degree": degree,
        "Major": "Unknown",  # Defaulting major to Unknown for simplicity
        "University": university,
        "Graduation Date": "Unknown",  # Defaulting Graduation Date to Unknown
        "LinkedIn": linkedin,
        "Skills": skills,
        "Experience": experience,
        "Education": education
    }

def extract_name(doc):
    for ent in doc.ents:
        if ent.label_ == "PERSON":
            name_parts = ent.text.split()
            return name_parts[0], name_parts[-1]  # Assume first and last name
    return "Unknown", "Unknown"

def extract_degree(text):
    degree_patterns = [r"(bachelor|master|phd|doctor)", r"(b.s.|m.s.|bs|ms)"]
    for pattern in degree_patterns:
        if re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):
            return "BS"  # Simplify to a single degree for now
    return "Unknown"

def extract_university(text):
    universities = ["University of California", "State University of New York"]
    for university in universities:
        if university.lower() in text.lower():
            return university
    return "Unknown"

def extract_linkedin(text):
    match = re.search(r"https?://(www\.)?linkedin\.com/in/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", text)
    return match.group(0) if match else "Unknown"

def extract_skills(text):
    skills = ["Python", "Java", "Machine Learning"]
    return [skill for skill in skills if skill.lower() in text.lower()]

def extract_section(text, section_name):
    pattern = re.compile(rf"({section_name}:)(.*?)(?=\n[A-Z])", re.DOTALL)
    match = re.search(pattern, text)
    if match:
        return match.group(2).strip()
    return "No content"

def format_filename(first_name, last_name, degree, university, file_path):
    grad_date = extract_graduation_date(file_path)
    filename = f"{last_name}, {first_name} - {degree} - {university} ({grad_date})"
    return "".join(c for c in filename if c not in "\\/:*?\"<>|")

def extract_graduation_date(file_path):
    # Example: May 2024 or Expected Graduation May 2024
    return "Unknown"

def save_parsed_data_to_csv(parsed_data):
    # Define the filename using the structured data
    filename = f"{parsed_data['Last Name']}, {parsed_data['First Name']} - {parsed_data['Degree']} - {parsed_data['Major']} - {parsed_data['University']} ({parsed_data['Graduation Date']}).csv"
    
    # Define the CSV file path
    csv_file_path = os.path.join(save_directory, filename)
    
    # Define CSV headers
    fieldnames = ["First Name", "Last Name", "Degree", "Major", "University", "Graduation Date", "LinkedIn", "Skills", "Experience", "Education"]
    
    # Create and write data to CSV
    with open(csv_file_path, mode='w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerow(parsed_data)
    print(f"CSV saved successfully: {csv_file_path}")

# Watchdog Event Handler for folder monitoring
class ResumeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        
        # Process the resume file when a new one is added to the folder
        print(f"New resume detected: {event.src_path}")
        
        # Check if the resume is scanned or digital
        if is_scanned(event.src_path):  # If scanned (image-based PDF or image file)
            process_scanned_resume(event.src_path)
        else:  # If digital (text-based PDF)
            process_digital_resume(event.src_path)

# Setup folder monitoring
def monitor_folder():
    event_handler = ResumeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, monitor_directory, recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor_folder()
